claim: Let \(H\) be the Heawood graph, realized as the point-line incidence graph of the Fano plane with points \(p_i\) and lines \(\ell_i\) for \(i\in\mathbb Z/7\mathbb Z\), where \(p_j\) is adjacent to \(\ell_i\) exactly when \(j-i\in\{0,1,3\}\). Then its independence complex satisfies \(\operatorname{Ind}(H)\simeq\bigvee^{6}S^{3}\).

correctness.rationale: The finite verifier reconstructs all 458 faces, confirms the published face counts, verifies a complete acyclic Hasse matching leaving exactly six critical 3-simplices and no other critical faces, and independently computes mod-2 Betti numbers (1,0,0,6,0,0,0). Discrete Morse theory then gives one 0-cell and six 3-cells, so the space is a wedge of six 3-spheres.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical 14-vertex cubic girth-six Moore graph and is already singled out in the literature as extremal for independent sets. Determining its full independence-complex homotopy type is a natural structural invariant, and the sharp contrast with the same-order same-degree cyclic-neighborhood graph G_7^3 shows that the result records topology not determined by coarse regular-bipartite parameters.
